chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ al-Madāʾinī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'How should one say salām to the people of the graves?' He replied: 'Say: Peace be upon the people of the dwellings, from among the believers and the Muslims. May Allah have mercy on those of you who preceded us and those who will follow, and we shall join you, if Allah wills.' Al-Barqī also narrated it from his father, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ al-Madāʾinī, who said: 'I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him),' and mentioned a similar narration.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الدِّيَارِ: People of the dwellings (a common euphemism for the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct formula for saying salam to the dead in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the standard liturgical formula for visiting graves, emphasizing the continuity of the believer's journey from this world to the next. It reflects the Shia theological concept of the 'Barzakh' (intermediate state), where the deceased remain conscious and connected to the living, reinforcing the communal bond of faith across time. The parallel narration via al-Barqī underscores the reliability and widespread acceptance of this specific phrasing in early Shia tradition.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. My father narrated to me from Ḥusain ibn Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Ḥusain ibn Sa’īd, from Naďr ibn Suwayd, from Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ Al-Madā`ini, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “How should one say Salām to the people of the graves?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Recite (the following):                   Salām upon the people of the graves from among the believers and the Muslims. May Allāh’s Mercy be upon those of you who died long ago and those of you who died recently. We shall join you In-Shā`allāh. The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated through the following chain: (Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad) Al-Barqi, from his father, from Naďr ibn Suwayd, from Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ Al-Madā`ini, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
